title: Canonical comparison of conductor-prepended towers
statement: Let $N$ be a smooth normalized resolution rule on all normal reduced finite-type rational schemes [def-trf-smooth-normalized-resolution-rule]. For a smooth map $h:Y\to X$ of reduced finite-type rational inputs and $A_X=N(P(X))$, $A_Y=N(P(Y))$ [def-trf-conductor-resolution-preparation], let $B_X,B_Y$ be their explicit conductor-extended towers [lem-trf-conductor-resolution-tower]. There exists a cartesian normalized resolution comparison $c$ from $B_Y$ to $B_X$ over $h$ [def-per-qe-normalized-resolution-rule]. For any other such comparison $d$, the contraction indices of $c,d$ agree at every original level and their actual surviving-level maps are heterogeneously equal. No identity, composition, surjectivity law or global resolution rule is asserted here.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 2.2.3--2.2.9 and 2.3.2--2.3.5(i), printed pp.90--93; agent formalization of the conductor-prepending refinement in the parent proof.

proof.text: Use the conductor smooth base-change square to obtain the unique smooth map P(Y) to P(X), and apply the supplied comparison of N to this map.

Handle the three conductor cases. Unit on X implies unit on Y and comparison is the rebased tail. If both are nonunit prepend the conductor square. If only Y is unit, prepend the pulled unit stage then delete its isomorphism over the normal Y. Shift the retained tail indices accordingly. The initial equations follow from the conductor square; subsequent cartesian, center and arrow equations are those of the supplied tail comparison. Each stage deleted is unit and an isomorphism; each other stage is retained in its original order.

Uniqueness of the retained-index map follows by recursion from its first value zero and whether each extended ideal is unit. Given the equal indices, equality of level maps is proved by induction: normalized blowup maps over a fixed preceding-level map agree over the dense complement of the center and hence on the reduced source, since the normalized blowup is separated over the preceding level. This determines exactly the maps used downstream, even if the auxiliary pulled models differ.

lean.statement:
theorem rationalConductorTower_comparison
    (N : SmoothNormalizedResolutionRule NormalRationalResolutionInput.{u}
      (fun X ↦ X.val.scheme))
    (X Y : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (h : Y.scheme ⟶ X.scheme) (hh : Smooth h) :
    ∃ c : QENormalizedResolutionComparison h
      (rationalConductorTower X (N.tower (normalConductorPreparedRationalInput X)))
      (rationalConductorTower Y (N.tower (normalConductorPreparedRationalInput Y))),
      ∀ d : QENormalizedResolutionComparison h
        (rationalConductorTower X (N.tower (normalConductorPreparedRationalInput X)))
        (rationalConductorTower Y (N.tower (normalConductorPreparedRationalInput Y))),
        (∀ i, d.contraction.index i = c.contraction.index i) ∧
          (∀ i, HEq (d.levelMap i) (c.levelMap i))
